items.prose: A lawn is a 10 m by 6 m rectangle with a semicircle on one 6 m side, as drawn.

state.caption: A 10 m by 6 m lawn with a semicircle on its right-hand side

parts.question: What is the area of the lawn, to 2 decimal places?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the rectangle and half a circle of radius 3.

byKey.full-circle: You added a whole circle. Only half of it is there.
byKey.diameter: You used 6 as the radius. The semicircle's diameter is 6, so its radius is 3.

explain.text: Rectangle $10 \times 6 = 60$ m². Semicircle $\tfrac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 3^2 = 4.5\pi \approx 14.14$ m². The lawn is about 74.14 m².

parts.question: What is the perimeter of the lawn, to 2 decimal places?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the three straight sides and the half circle; the dashed side is inside.

byKey.shared: You counted the dashed 6 m side. It is inside the lawn, not on its edge.
byKey.full: You used a full circle's rim. Only half is on the edge.
byKey.no-arc: You left out the curved edge, $3\pi$.

explain.text: The edge is 10 m, 6 m and 10 m of straight side and half of $\pi \times 6$, which is $3\pi \approx 9.42$ m. In all, $26 + 3\pi \approx 35.42$ m.

explain.text: Total $1 \times 3 + 2 \times 6 + 3 \times 7 + 4 \times 4 = 52$ orders over 20 hours, so the mean is 2.6.

parts.question: What is the median number of orders an hour?

feedback.correct: The 10th and 11th hours in order both had 3 orders.

items.prose: Eight traders' bonuses average £45,000. The trader with the largest bonus, £87,000, leaves the desk.
items.question: What is the mean bonus of the seven who stay?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the total for eight, take away £87,000, then share over seven.

byKey.unchanged: Removing a bonus above the mean lowers the mean.
byKey.eight: You still divided by 8. Seven traders are left.
byKey.old-total: You divided the old total by 7. Take the £87,000 out first.

explain.text: Eight bonuses averaging £45,000 total £360,000. Without the £87,000, seven bonuses total £273,000, so their mean is $273{,}000 \div 7 = 39{,}000$ pounds.

items.prose: Find the HCF of 1,071 and 462 without splitting either into primes.
items.question: Put the steps of Euclid's method in order. Leave out the line that does not follow.

lines.text: The last remainder before 0 is 21, so the HCF of 1,071 and 462 is 21.
Check: $1{,}071 = 21 \times 51$ and $462 = 21 \times 22$, and 51 and 22 share no prime.
The first remainder is 147, so the HCF of 1,071 and 462 is 147.
lines.why: 147 does not divide 462: $3 \times 147 = 441$ leaves 21. Carry on until nothing is left.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each step works on the smaller number and the remainder from the step before.

byKey.bad: 147 is only the first remainder. It does not divide 462.

explain.text: Each step keeps every common factor, because what divides both numbers divides the remainder. The remainders run 147, 21, 0, so the HCF is 21. Then the LCM is $21 \times 51 \times 22 = 23{,}562$.

items.title: A broker's leaflet
items.prompt:
A broker's leaflet shows last year's monthly profits as a bar chart whose axis starts at £15,000. It says: "Average monthly profit: £35,000." The figures, in thousands of pounds, were: Jan 18, Feb 22, Mar 20, Apr 19, May 21, Jun 20, Jul 23, Aug 17, Sep 20, Oct 22, Nov 18, Dec 200.

Say what the chart and the quoted mean each hide. Check the mean, find the median, and write an honest one-paragraph description of a typical month.
items.model:
**What the chart hides.** The axis starts at £15,000, not at 0. A month of £20,000 then shows only £5,000 of bar and a month of £23,000 shows £8,000. So a month that is 1.15 times another looks 1.6 times as big. The December bar, £200,000, runs far off the top of the others.

**What the mean hides.** The twelve months add to

$$\begin{aligned} &18 + 22 + 20 + 19 + 21 + 20 \\ &+ 23 + 17 + 20 + 22 + 18 + 200 = 420 \end{aligned}$$

thousand pounds, so the mean is $420 \div 12 = 35$, which is £35,000. Eleven of the twelve months made £23,000 or less. The one December month of £200,000 drags the mean up: without it the other eleven average $220 \div 11 = 20$, which is £20,000.

**The median.** Sorted: 17, 18, 18, 19, 20, 20, 20, 21, 22, 22, 23, 200. Twelve values have two middle ones, the 6th and 7th, both 20. So the median is £20,000.

**An honest description.** "In a typical month last year the fund made about £20,000 (median); eleven months fell between £17,000 and £23,000. One exceptional month made £200,000, which lifts the mean to £35,000. The chart's axis should start at £0, with the December figure marked as an outlier."

**Which number answers what.** The mean, £35,000, is right if you want the year's total spread over twelve months: $12 \times 35{,}000 = 420{,}000$. The median answers "what does a usual month look like", and says £20,000.

rubric.text: Explains that an axis starting at £15,000 exaggerates differences between months, with an example from the figures.
Checks the mean: a total of £420,000 over 12 months gives £35,000.
Names December's £200,000, about ten times a usual month, as the value that pulls the mean up.
Sorts the twelve values and takes the mean of the 6th and 7th to get a median of £20,000.
Writes an honest description using the median, the usual range of months and the outlier, with an axis from £0.
Says what the mean does answer: the year's total shared over twelve months.

items.prose: 2,520 is the smallest number that every whole number from 1 to 10 divides.
items.question: How many factors does 2,520 have?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write 2,520 as a product of primes, add 1 to each index and multiply.

byKey.added: You added the indices. Add 1 to each, then multiply.
byKey.no-plus-one: You multiplied the indices. Add 1 to each first.
byKey.added-plus: You added the choices. Multiply them.

explain.text: $2{,}520 = 8 \times 315 = 2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5 \times 7$. The choices are 4, 3, 2 and 2, so 2,520 has $4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 2 = 48$ factors.
